note: Adapted from the species description of Sjöstedt (1900), originally in Latin and German; the original treats only the alate, the soldier and worker not being described; the Latin passage is incomplete owing to OCR damage and was checked against the German passage; measurements, figure numbers and locality records are not transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Closely related to Eutermes arboricola but slightly smaller; the wing venation, especially towards the outer margin, is much less distinct than in that species; body smaller and narrower; legs without dark shading; the first two teeth of the mandibles almost equal in size, whereas the first tooth of E. arboricola is much larger.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown above; head scarcely darker than the body, densely covered with fine hairs, about as wide as the distance between the tips of the compound eyes, vertex very slightly concave, fontanelle absent or almost indiscernible; slightly raised between the compound eyes, with an indistinct small depression running inward from each ocellus; clypeus not much inflated, reddish, paler than the frons; compound eyes large, prominent; ocelli separated from the compound eyes by slightly less than their own diameter; antennae 15-segmented, yellowish, with darker annuli; first segment slightly widened upwards, third segment small, the following segments more rounded, slightly elongate towards the antennal apex, apical segment elongate-oval; pronotum very small, as wide as the head without the compound eyes, semicircular, rather broadly flattened and slightly concave posteriorly; anterior margin almost straight, raised in a saddle; anterior angles slightly deflexed, rounded and slightly concave; mesonotum narrowed posteriorly, with two short pointed projections, the projections on the metanotum smaller; wings long and narrow, rounded apically, more than four times as long as wide, pale brownish grey; costa and subcosta darker, parallel; media running straight to the wing apex slightly above the middle and dividing into three branches; media and submedia slowly diverging outwards; submedia with 7–9 branches; veins distinct but only near the base; abdominal tergites pale coriaceous brown, with dark shading laterally, the sixth abdominal segment of the female very large, nearly semicircular; legs, mouthparts and maxillary palps dirty white, tinged yellowish brown, extending beyond the abdominal apex; last tarsomere slightly longer than the remaining tarsomeres together; claws and tibial spines dark brown; whole body densely covered with fine hairs.
